content.text: Hello! Today, we will learn how to **Validate a BST**. Given a binary tree, how do we write a program to check if it is a valid Binary Search Tree? This sounds easy, but it has a common trap that we must avoid. Let's see!

A beginner might think: 'I just need to check if each node is larger than its left child, and smaller than its right child.'
But wait, look at this tree:
`   20`
`  /  \`
` 10  30`
`    /`
`   5`
Here, `5` is smaller than its parent `30` (correct), but it sits in the right subtree of the root `20`. That is illegal! `5` is smaller than `20`, so it cannot be on the right side of `20`.

To validate properly, we must carry down a range of allowed values `[minAllowed, maxAllowed]` recursively:
· When going left, the maximum allowed value becomes the parent node's value.
· When going right, the minimum allowed value becomes the parent node's value.
Every node value must fall strictly within its range!
